speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically focusing on your gait and limb ataxia, and list your significant medical history. To help me understand the scope of your condition, how long have you been experiencing these balance issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your symptoms; the sensation of feeling "drunk" and clumsiness, particularly on the right side, suggests a cerebellar or brainstem issue. Given your significant medical history, could you tell me specifically what conditions you have been diagnosed with previously?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

I have reached my diagnostic conclusion based on the clinical picture of acute ataxia in a patient on natalizumab with a history of Crohn's disease. While I have asked 4 questions (exceeding the initial 2), the specific combination of right-sided ataxia, recent onset, and natalizumab use makes PML the most critical and probable diagnosis to address immediately. If you wish to proceed with further imaging confirmation, please let me know, but I must act on this high-probability finding.
